data.gender_notes: Andromada is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: In Greek mythology, Andromeda was a beautiful princess chained to a rock as a sacrifice to a sea monster.
data.long_meaning: Andromeda was the name of a beautiful princess in Greek mythology, daughter of Cassiopeia and Cepheus. She was punished by the gods for boasting about her beauty. To appease the sea god Poseidon, her mother was forced to sacrifice her to a sea monster. The monster was averted, however, when Perseus arrived and saved Andromeda, making her his wife.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of redemption and the courage to overcome adversity.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Andromada total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Christianizing the name "Andromeda" is an imaginative adaptation, as it originates from ancient Greek mythology. While preserving its ancient roots, this name undergoes spiritual transformation by connoting womanhood draped in divine strength and wisdom. With an inspirational backdrop of a tragic tale of sacrifice and redemption, the Christian name "Andromeda" proudly echoes the stories of faith, hope, and courage in the bible.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Andromeda" in a Christian context symbolizes the strength and resilience of a faithful heart in the face of trials and tribulations. Herstory carries a powerful message: no trial or tribulation (sea monster) is insurmountable when love, courage, and faith guide us. This inspires us to look beyond personal struggles and embrace our divine purpose - being fearlessly devoted to our Creator.
